clue.text: Made keen, but went cautiously

definitions.meaning: to put a sharp cutting rim on a blade, past tense
moved sideways little by little, as along a ledge

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one verb: sharpened a blade, and crept forward bit by bit.

clue.text: Classy writer about to be introduced to darling French composer

indicators.note: being introduced to something means going inside it, so these letters sit within the French word

parts.note: cheri is French for darling
U is the old label for upper-class, posh usage

indicators.note: about signals turning the pen-point word round so it reads backwards

parts.note: a nib is the writing point of a pen

explanation.surface: A posh author is about to meet a beloved French composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives BIN. Cherubini was Italian-born but spent his career in Paris, which is why the surface can call him French.
explanation.definitionFit: Luigi Cherubini was an operatic and sacred-music composer of the Classical era.

clue.text: Husband, initially dull and prosaic, turning out effusively eloquent

indicators.note: turning out suggests the letters being turned over into a new form, an anagram signal
initially picks the opening letter of the word dull

parts.note: taken as written as part of the fodder

explanation.surface: A dull, matter-of-fact husband unexpectedly becomes a gushing speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning out' rearranges H, D and PROSAIC together.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhapsodic speech is ecstatic and gushing, which is what effusively eloquent describes.

clue.text: Poet's winter coat

definitions.meaning: Robert ..., the American poet of New England
the white covering of ice crystals on cold winter mornings

explanation.definitionFit: Robert Frost was an American poet, and a hoar layer of ice coats things in winter.

clue.text: Molly's last word, husband being an agreeable type

parts.note: Molly Bloom's soliloquy ending Joyce's Ulysses closes on the word yes
man as in man and wife

explanation.surface: A wife's final word, with her husband going along with everything.
explanation.walkthrough: Molly Bloom's famous monologue at the end of James Joyce's Ulysses finishes 'yes I said yes I will Yes'.
explanation.definitionFit: A yes-man always agrees with his superiors, a compliant and agreeable sort.

clue.text: One providing delicacies; operator eats tons

indicators.note: eats means taking something in, so the operator word swallows the letter

parts.note: a surgeon operates on patients

explanation.surface: A surgeon with an enormous appetite gets through tons of food.
explanation.walkthrough: The fish's roe is caviar, the delicacy in question.
explanation.definitionFit: This fish's roe is caviar, so it is a source of luxury food.

clue.text: In which I should never appear to drop luggage

definitions.text: In which I should never appear

parts.note: to lower is to drop or let down
a case is a suitcase

explanation.surface: Somewhere a person must never be seen, then a bag being let fall.
explanation.walkthrough: The personal pronoun I is always written as a capital, so it never appears in small letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Small letters are those other than capitals, and the pronoun I is always capitalised.

clue.text: Philosopher endlessly banal, one admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so the numeral goes inside the shortened word
endlessly means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: stock as in a stock phrase, trite and banal
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A philosopher, tediously dull, is let in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts STOCK to STOC; 'admitted' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stoic was a follower of Zeno's school of philosophy in ancient Greece.

clue.text: Music critic marks ancient instrument

parts.note: George Bernard Shaw wrote music criticism in London before his plays made him famous
M is the abbreviation for marks, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A music reviewer scores an old instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: Shaw reviewed concerts under the pen name Corno di Bassetto.
explanation.definitionFit: A shawm is a medieval double-reed woodwind, forerunner of the oboe.

clue.text: Refusal by festival to admit monarch is a blow

parts.note: no is a refusal
R stands for rex or regina, king or queen
Easter is a Christian festival

explanation.surface: Being turned down for a festival that will not let the king in is a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is a blow' looks like 'is a setback', but a blow here is a gale.
explanation.definitionFit: A nor'easter is a strong gale from the north-east, and a blow is a storm of wind.

clue.text: In symbols, write down almost everything? The opposite

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to notate is to record in symbols, as music is
all means everything

explanation.surface: Asked whether to record absolutely everything in symbols, the answer is no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims NOTATE to NOTAT. The phrase meaning 'in no way' is the opposite of 'everything'.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaning nothing whatever, the phrase is the reverse of saying everything, as the clue's question asks.

clue.text: I bleed badly, but it's not hurting to swallow

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters are messed up, an anagram signal

explanation.surface: Someone bleeding badly insists the thing they are eating does no harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges I BLEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Edible food is safe to eat, causing no harm when swallowed.

clue.text: Plan to eliminate singular stoop

indicators.note: to eliminate means to take out, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a design is a plan
S is the grammar abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A scheme to cut out one thing comes down low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stoop' is a verb here, to lower oneself, not a bent posture.
explanation.definitionFit: To deign is to condescend, to stoop to doing something beneath one's dignity.

clue.text: Some cricket a laugh? That's to go too far

parts.note: overs are sets of six balls bowled in cricket
a hoot is something very funny

explanation.surface: A spell of cricket is hilarious, but taking it further is excessive.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: To overshoot is to go past a target, exceeding the intended limit.

clue.text: Standard credit extends some distance

indicators.note: extends means the credit word is added on to make the distance longer

parts.note: yards are a measure of distance
tick is British slang for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: Credit is lengthened over some way, a benchmark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On tick' is British slang for 'on credit'.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardstick is a measure or benchmark for comparison, a standard.

clue.text: Retreat backed to protect country devastatingly attacked

indicators.note: to protect is to surround, so the reversed word encloses the country
backed means turned backwards

parts.note: a den is a private retreat
UK is the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: A retreat backs up to shield a nation savagely assaulted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' gives NED; 'to protect' here means wrapping round, not shielding from harm.
explanation.definitionFit: To nuke is to strike with nuclear weapons, the most devastating attack.

clue.text: On which no purchases can be made beyond, say, one

definitions.text: On which no purchases can be made beyond, say, one

parts.words: On which no purchases can be made beyond, say, one
parts.note: one o'clock in the afternoon, after which shops in a British town once shut for the half-day

explanation.walkthrough: British towns used to have one weekday when shops shut at about 1pm; 'one' is a time, not a number of purchases.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the weekly half-day when local shops closed in the afternoon, so nothing could be bought after lunch.

clue.text: Main constituent of lawn is weed

definitions.meaning: the green blades that make up a lawn
slang for cannabis, also called pot

explanation.definitionFit: Lawns are mostly turf plants, and the same word is slang for cannabis.

clue.text: Bunyan's giant aspired to reform

indicators.note: to reform is to form again differently, an anagram signal

explanation.surface: The giant in Bunyan's tale wished to change his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reform' rearranges ASPIRED. In Bunyan's Pilgrim's Progress, Giant Despair imprisons Christian in Doubting Castle.
explanation.definitionFit: Giant Despair is the ogre of Doubting Castle in John Bunyan's allegory The Pilgrim's Progress.

clue.text: Established standards in school ultimately switched

indicators.note: the final pair of letters are switched round, reading backwards

parts.note: coed is short for a coeducational school

explanation.surface: Accepted norms are changed at a school in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately switched' swaps the last two letters of COED.
explanation.definitionFit: A code is a set of rules or conventions accepted as standard.

clue.text: Officially not hard to spell "Worcester," for example, but not finishing

indicators.note: not hard means the letter for hard is taken away from the spell

parts.note: a hex is a magic spell
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: not finishing means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Worcester has a famous cathedral, standing for the building

explanation.surface: Spelling Worcester is not, officially, difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: HEX loses H to give EX; 'not finishing' cuts CATHEDRAL to CATHEDRA. Worcester is an English city with a cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: Ex cathedra means from the chair of office, so spoken with official authority.

clue.text: Warm coat left in boiling sun spreads open

indicators.note: in places the coat and left inside the scrambled sun
boiling suggests churning, an anagram signal

parts.note: fur is a warm coat

explanation.surface: Under a blazing sun, a warm coat left behind is laid out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boiling' rearranges SUN as UNS; 'in' puts FURL inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfurl a flag or sail is to unroll it so that it spreads out.

clue.text: Very hard internet query, could one say, in absence of book is cleared up

parts.note: iron is proverbially very hard, as in an iron will

indicators.note: in absence of means the book letter is taken out

parts.note: a playful coinage, an electronic doubt, by analogy with e-mail

explanation.surface: A tough online question, missing a book, is resolved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could one say' admits E-DOUBT is invented; without B it gives EDOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Problems that are ironed out are smoothed away and resolved, like creases.

clue.text: You're right, it's wrong — and fixed

definitions.text: You're right, it's wrong — and fixed

parts.words: You're right, it's wrong — and fixed
parts.note: an admission of being mistaken, read also as a speaker literally put right and set firmly in place

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase concedes an error; read literally, the speaker is both upright and amended.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the stock concession made when someone shows that one has erred.

clue.text: Pasta new local in NE might serve

indicators.note: might serve suggests the letters being dished up in another order

explanation.surface: A new pub in the North East might serve pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might serve' rearranges N with LOCAL IN NE. A local is British slang for a neighbourhood pub; NE is the North East of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannelloni are large pasta tubes, usually stuffed and baked.

clue.text: At first, whippet thriving more without lead — it's better off

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letter of whippet
without lead means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: healthier means thriving more

explanation.surface: A whippet off its leash is doing better than before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without lead' cuts HEALTHIER to EALTHIER. 'Lead' suggests a dog's leash, not the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wealthier means having more money, so financially better off.

clue.text: Dogs retain a passion ultimately for sports

indicators.note: to retain is to hold within, so the dogs enclose the letters

parts.note: mutts are mongrel dogs

indicators.note: ultimately picks the last letter of passion

explanation.surface: Dogs keep a passion for sports in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sports' is the biology sense, an animal or plant unlike its parents, not games.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology a sport is an organism showing a sudden variation, the same as a mutant.

clue.text: Essayist's advice to extend family?

parts.note: said aloud, the writer's surname runs together as a suggestion to have one more boy

explanation.walkthrough: Joseph Addison was the English essayist behind The Spectator; his name, run together in speech, sounds like 'add a son'.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Addison was an early-18th-century English writer known for his periodical essays.

clue.text: Badger bishop to be really exciting

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to rock is to be great, exciting

explanation.surface: Pester a bishop to liven things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badger' looks like the verb, to pester, but is the animal: Brock is the traditional English name for a badger.
explanation.definitionFit: In English folklore the badger is called Brock, so the name is a by-name for the animal.

clue.text: Picked up needle point

indicators.note: picked up as in heard, signalling a word that sounds the same

parts.note: pique is irritation, what someone feels when needled

explanation.surface: A needle's sharp end is lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' means heard here, not lifted.
explanation.definitionFit: A peak is the pointed top of a mountain, a point.
